EVAL: cg2-e01
Implement `sumOfEvens`: return the sum of all even numbers in the integer array nums. An integer n is even when n % 2 === 0; negative even numbers (e.g. -4) must be included in the sum, and 0 is even. Return 0 for an empty array or when no even numbers are present.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cg2-e02
Implement `secondLargest`: return the second-largest distinct value in the integer array nums. Duplicates do not create extra ranks: for [5, 5, 3] the answer is 3. If the array has fewer than two distinct values (empty array, single element, or all elements equal), return null.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cg2-e03
Implement `reverseWords`: given a string s, return its words in reverse order joined by single spaces. Words are maximal runs of non-whitespace characters; any run of spaces or tabs separates words. Leading and trailing whitespace must not produce empty words. Return an empty string for an empty or whitespace-only input.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cg2-e04
Implement `clampAll`: return a NEW array where every number in nums is clamped into the inclusive range [lo, hi]: values below lo become lo, values above hi become hi, and values already inside the range (including exactly lo or hi) are unchanged. Do not mutate the input array. Return [] for an empty array. Bounds may be negative.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cg2-e05
Implement `isPalindromeLoose`: return true if string s is a palindrome when considering only ASCII letters and digits and ignoring letter case; every other character is skipped. A string with no letters or digits at all (including the empty string) counts as a palindrome and returns true.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cg2-e06
Implement `firstUniqueChar`: return the first character of string s (case-sensitive, so 'a' and 'A' are different characters) that occurs exactly once in the whole string. If every character repeats or the string is empty, return the empty string ''.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cg2-e07
Implement `digitSum`: return the sum of the decimal digits of the integer n. For negative n, use the digits of its absolute value, so digitSum(-456) === 15. digitSum(0) must return 0.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cg2-e08
Implement `longestWord`: return the longest word of string s, where words are maximal runs of non-whitespace characters (punctuation stays attached to its word). If several words tie for the longest length, return the one that appears first. Return '' for an empty or whitespace-only string.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cg2-e09
Implement `removeDuplicates`: return a new array containing the elements of arr with duplicates removed, keeping only the FIRST occurrence of each value and preserving order. Equality is strict (===), so the number 1 and the string '1' are different values. Return [] for an empty array; do not mutate the input.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cg2-e10
Implement `countBetween`: return how many elements x of the number array nums satisfy lo <= x <= hi (both bounds inclusive). If lo > hi, return 0. Return 0 for an empty array. Bounds and elements may be negative.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cg2-e11
Implement `padNumber`: return the integer n as a decimal string left-padded with '0' characters to a total length of width. If the plain decimal string already has length greater than or equal to width, return it unchanged. For negative n the minus sign comes first and counts toward the width: padNumber(-5, 4) === '-005'.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cg2-e12
Implement `median`: return the median of the number array nums: sort a COPY numerically (not lexicographically - [10, 9, 80] has median 10), then return the middle element for odd length or the average of the two middle elements for even length. Return null for an empty array and do not mutate the input.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cg2-e13
Implement `truncateWords`: return the first n words of string s joined by single spaces, where words are maximal runs of non-whitespace characters (extra spaces are collapsed). If n <= 0 return ''. If s has fewer than n words, return all of them. Return '' for an empty or whitespace-only string.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cg2-e14
Implement `countUppercase`: return the number of ASCII uppercase letters (A-Z) in string s. Digits, punctuation, spaces and lowercase letters are not counted. Return 0 for an empty string.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cg2-e15
Implement `maxDiff`: return the difference between the maximum and minimum values of the number array nums (max minus min). If the array has fewer than two elements, return 0. Works with negative numbers; an array of all-equal values returns 0.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cg2-e16
Implement `wordsStartingWith`: return a new array of the strings in words (in original order and original casing) whose lowercase form starts with the lowercase form of prefix. The empty prefix matches every word. Return [] for an empty words array or when nothing matches.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cg2-e17
Implement `swapCase`: return string s with the case of every ASCII letter swapped: uppercase A-Z become lowercase and lowercase a-z become uppercase. Digits, punctuation, and spaces are unchanged. Return '' for an empty string.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cg2-e18
Implement `lastIndexOfMax`: return the index of the LAST occurrence of the maximum value in the number array nums (when the maximum appears several times, pick the highest index). Return -1 for an empty array. Works with negative numbers.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cg2-e19
Implement `chunkArray`: split arr into consecutive chunks of length size and return them as an array of arrays; the final chunk may be shorter when the length is not divisible by size. If size <= 0 return []. Return [] for an empty input array. Do not mutate the input.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cg2-e20
Implement `areAnagrams`: return true if strings a and b are anagrams ignoring letter case and ignoring space characters: after lowercasing and removing spaces, both must contain exactly the same characters with the same multiplicities (digits and punctuation DO count). Two strings that are both empty or contain only spaces are anagrams.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cg2-m01
Implement `mergeIntervals`: given an array of integer intervals [start, end] with start <= end, in arbitrary order, merge every group of intervals that overlap or touch (e.g. [1,2] and [2,3] merge into [1,3]; a fully nested interval is absorbed) and return the merged intervals as new [start, end] pairs sorted by start. Return [] for an empty input. Do not mutate the input array or its inner pairs.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cg2-m02
Implement `twoSumIndices`: given a number array nums and a number target, find two indices i < j with nums[i] + nums[j] === target. Scan j from left to right and for each j prefer the smallest valid i; return the first such pair found as [i, j] (i.e. the pair with the smallest j, breaking ties by smallest i). Return null if no pair exists. The same element may not be used twice, but two equal values at different indices may be (e.g. [3,3] with target 6 gives [0,1]). Values may be negative.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cg2-m03
Implement `isBalancedBrackets`: return true if the brackets in string s are balanced. Only the six characters ()[]{} are considered; every other character is ignored. Balanced means every opening bracket is closed by the matching closing bracket in the correct nesting order (so '([)]' is NOT balanced). An empty string or a string with no brackets returns true.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cg2-m04
Implement `runLengthEncode`: run-length encode string s: replace each maximal run of a repeated character with the character followed by the run length in decimal, ALWAYS including the count even when it is 1, so 'aaabccc' becomes 'a3b1c3' and 'abc' becomes 'a1b1c1'. Comparison is case-sensitive ('a' and 'A' are different runs). Runs longer than 9 produce multi-digit counts. Return '' for an empty string.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cg2-m05
Implement `spiralOrder`: given a rectangular matrix (array of rows, all rows the same length), return a flat array of its elements visited in clockwise spiral order starting at the top-left: top row left-to-right, then right column top-to-bottom, then bottom row right-to-left, then left column bottom-to-top, then inward. Must handle a single row, a single column, and non-square shapes; return [] for an empty matrix [].

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cg2-m06
Implement `intToBase`: convert the integer n to its string representation in the given base (2 to 16), using digits 0-9 then lowercase letters a-f. intToBase(0, base) === '0' for any base. For negative n return '-' followed by the representation of the absolute value.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cg2-m07
Implement `dayOfYear`: return the 1-based day-of-year ordinal for the calendar date given as year y, month m (1-12) and day d, without using the Date object. Leap years have a 29-day February: a year is a leap year when divisible by 4, EXCEPT century years, which are leap only when divisible by 400 (2000 was a leap year, 1900 was not). So dayOfYear(2000, 3, 1) === 61 while dayOfYear(1900, 3, 1) === 60.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cg2-m08
Implement `longestUniqueSubstring`: return the length of the longest contiguous substring of s in which no character appears more than once (case-sensitive). Return 0 for the empty string. Example: for 'abcabcbb' the answer is 3 ('abc'); for 'abba' the answer is 2 - the sliding window must restart correctly after a repeat.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cg2-m09
Implement `sortByFrequency`: return a new array with the elements of the number array nums sorted by descending frequency (most common values first); when two distinct values have the same frequency, the smaller value comes first; equal values stay adjacent. Example: [4,4,1,2,2,2] becomes [2,2,2,4,4,1]. Return [] for an empty array; do not mutate the input.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cg2-m10
Implement `rotateMatrix`: rotate a rectangular matrix (array of R rows, each an array of C numbers) 90 degrees clockwise and return the result as a NEW C-by-R matrix, where output[i][j] === input[R-1-j][i]. Do not mutate the input. Works for non-square matrices and a 1x1 matrix; return [] for an empty matrix [].

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cg2-m11
Implement `evaluateRPN`: evaluate an arithmetic expression in Reverse Polish Notation. tokens is an array of strings, each either an integer (possibly negative, like '-3') or one of the operators '+', '-', '*', '/'. Each operator pops the two most recent operands and pushes the result; the second-popped value is the left operand (so ['5','3','-'] is 5 - 3 = 2). Division truncates toward zero: 7 / -3 evaluates to -2. The expression is always valid; return the resulting number.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cg2-m12
Implement `mergeSortedArrays`: merge two ascending-sorted number arrays a and b into one ascending-sorted array containing every element of both, using a single left-to-right two-pointer pass. All duplicates are kept; when the next candidates are equal, take the one from a first. Either or both inputs may be empty. Do not mutate the inputs.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cg2-m13
Implement `compressRanges`: given a strictly increasing array of integers, return a comma-separated string where each maximal run of consecutive integers (each element exactly one greater than the previous) of length two or more is written as 'first-last', and isolated values are written alone. Example: [1,2,3,5,7,8,9] gives '1-3,5,7-9'. Negative values are allowed ([-3,-2,-1] gives '-3--1'). Return '' for an empty array.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cg2-m14
Implement `anagramGroups`: group the strings in words into anagram groups: two words belong to the same group when they contain exactly the same characters with the same counts (case-sensitive). Return an array of groups (arrays of strings); groups appear in order of the first occurrence of any of their members, and within a group words keep their original relative order (duplicates stay). Return [] for an empty input; the empty string is an anagram of the empty string.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cg2-m15
Implement `caesarCipher`: apply a Caesar cipher to string s: shift every ASCII letter forward by shift alphabet positions, wrapping around the alphabet and preserving case; every non-letter character is unchanged. shift can be any integer - negative shifts go backwards ('a' shifted by -1 is 'z') and shifts are taken modulo 26 (shift 27 equals shift 1; shift 52 leaves the string unchanged).

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cg2-m16
Implement `topKFrequentWords`: return the k most frequent strings in the array words, ordered by descending frequency; strings with equal frequency are ordered lexicographically ascending (standard < comparison). If k is greater than the number of distinct strings, return all distinct strings in that order. Return [] when k <= 0 or words is empty.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cg2-m17
Implement `addBigStrings`: add two non-negative integers given as decimal strings a and b (each may be hundreds of digits long, no signs, no leading zeros except the string '0' itself) and return their sum as a decimal string with no leading zeros. Handle carries across all digit positions ('999' + '1' === '1000') and inputs of different lengths. Do not convert the whole strings to numbers.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cg2-m18
Implement `maxSumWindow`: return the maximum sum over all contiguous windows of exactly k elements of the number array nums, computed with a sliding window. Return null when k <= 0 or k > nums.length. Elements may be negative (for an all-negative array the answer is the largest window sum, which is still negative).

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cg2-m19
Implement `parseQueryString`: parse the query string qs (no leading question mark, no URL decoding) into a plain object. Split qs on '&'; skip empty segments (produced by '' or '&&'). Each segment splits at its FIRST '=' into key and value ('a=b=c' gives key 'a' with value 'b=c'); a segment without '=' is a key with value ''. A key appearing exactly once maps to its string value; a key appearing multiple times maps to an array of all its values in order. Return an empty object for the empty string.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cg2-m20
Implement `pascalRow`: return row n (0-indexed) of Pascal's triangle as an array of integers: pascalRow(0) is [1], pascalRow(1) is [1,1], pascalRow(4) is [1,4,6,4,1]; each interior entry is the sum of the two entries above it. Return [] for negative n. Results must be exact integers for n up to at least 25 (build additively, do not use floating-point factorial division).

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cg2-m21
Implement `countIslands`: count the islands in a grid given as an array of rows of the numbers 0 and 1. An island is a maximal group of 1-cells connected horizontally or vertically (NOT diagonally). Return 0 for an empty grid ([]). Do not mutate the grid.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cg2-m22
Implement `romanToInt`: convert a valid Roman numeral string (characters I=1, V=5, X=10, L=50, C=100, D=500, M=1000) to its integer value, handling the six subtractive pairs IV=4, IX=9, XL=40, XC=90, CD=400, CM=900: whenever a symbol of smaller value appears immediately before one of larger value, it is subtracted instead of added. Example: 'MCMXCIV' is 1994.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cg2-m23
Implement `excelColumn`: convert the positive integer n to its spreadsheet column label using bijective base-26 with uppercase letters: 1 is 'A', 26 is 'Z', 27 is 'AA', 52 is 'AZ', 703 is 'AAA'. Note there is no zero digit, so plain base-26 conversion gives the wrong answer at multiples of 26. Return '' when n < 1.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cg2-m24
Implement `addDaysToDate`: given a valid Gregorian calendar date as year y, month m (1-12), day d, and a non-negative integer n, return the date n days later as an array [year, month, day], WITHOUT using the Date object. Leap years have a 29-day February: divisible by 4, except century years which must be divisible by 400 (2020 and 2000 are leap years, 2019 and 1900 are not). Handle month and year rollover; n === 0 returns the same date.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cg2-m25
Implement `minRooms`: meetings are given as an array of intervals [start, end) - each occupies times from start inclusive to end exclusive, so a meeting ending at time t and another starting at time t can share a room. Return the minimum number of rooms needed to hold all meetings, i.e. the maximum number of meetings in progress at any instant. Return 0 for an empty array.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cg2-h01
Implement `editDistance`: given two strings `a` and `b`, return the Levenshtein edit distance between them: the minimum number of single-character insertions, deletions, or substitutions needed to transform `a` into `b`. Return a number.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cg2-h02
Implement `coinChangeCombinations`: given an array `coins` of distinct positive integer denominations and a non-negative integer `amount`, return the number of distinct combinations of coins that sum to `amount`. Each denomination may be used any number of times, and order does not matter (using a 2 then a 3 is the same combination as a 3 then a 2). If `amount` is 0 there is exactly one combination: the empty one. Return a number.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cg2-h03
Implement `longestIncreasingLength`: given an array `nums` of integers, return the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence (elements keep their original relative order but need not be contiguous; equal adjacent values do NOT count as increasing). Return 0 for an empty array. Return a number.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cg2-h04
Implement `countNQueensSolutions`: given a positive integer `n`, return the number of distinct ways to place `n` queens on an `n` x `n` chessboard so that no two queens attack each other (no shared row, column, or diagonal). Distinct board arrangements count separately even if related by rotation or reflection. Return a number.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cg2-h05
Implement `hasSubsetSum`: given an array `nums` of positive integers and a non-negative integer `target`, return true if some subset of `nums` (each element used at most once; the empty subset is allowed and sums to 0) sums exactly to `target`, and false otherwise. Return a boolean.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cg2-h06
Implement `evalArithmetic`: given a string `expr` containing a valid arithmetic expression made of non-negative integer literals, the binary operators + - * /, parentheses, and optional spaces, return its numeric value. * and / have higher precedence than + and -; operators of equal precedence associate left to right; parentheses override precedence. Use ordinary floating-point division (e.g. 5/2 is 2.5). The input is always a well-formed expression with no unary operators. Do NOT use eval or the Function constructor. Return a number.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

EVAL: cg2-h07
Implement `parseCsvLine`: given a single CSV record as a string `line` (no newline characters), return an array of its field strings. Fields are separated by commas. A field may be enclosed in double quotes; inside a quoted field, commas are literal characters and a pair of double quotes "" represents one literal double-quote character. The enclosing quotes are not part of the field value. Unquoted fields are taken verbatim. An empty string is one empty field, so return [""]. Assume the input is well-formed. Return an array of strings.

Return 0 if `start` equals `end`, and -1 if `end` is unreachable from `start`. A name that appears as a neighbor but not as a key has no outgoing edges. Return a number.

Implement `hasDirectedCycle`: given a directed graph as an object `graph` mapping each node name (string) to an array of neighbor node names, return true if the graph contains at least one directed cycle (a self-loop counts), and false otherwise. Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

Implement `isValidTopoOrder`: given a directed acyclic graph as an object `graph` mapping each node name (string) to an array of neighbor node names (every neighbor is guaranteed to also be a key of `graph`), and an array `order` of node names, return true if `order` is a valid topological ordering of the graph: it contains every key of `graph` exactly once and nothing else, and for every edge u -> v, u appears before v in `order`. Return a boolean.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

Implement `minParenRemovals`: given a string `s` consisting only of the characters '(' and ')', return the minimum number of characters that must be removed so that the remaining string is balanced (every '(' has a matching later ')', and pairs nest properly; the empty string is balanced). Return a number.

Respond with ONLY the JavaScript function source, no markdown fences, no explanation.

Implement `maxNonOverlappingIntervals`: given an array `intervals` of two-element arrays [start, end] with start < end (numbers, in no particular order), return the maximum number of intervals you can select so that no two selected intervals overlap. Implement `countStairWays`: given a non-negative integer `n` and an array `steps` of distinct positive integers, return the number of distinct ordered sequences of values taken from `steps` (values may repeat within a sequence) whose sum is exactly `n`. Implement `longestPalindromicSubseqLength`: given a string `s`, return the length of the longest palindromic subsequence of `s` (a subsequence keeps character order but need not be contiguous; a palindrome reads the same forwards and backwards; a single character is a palindrome). Return 0 for the empty string. Return a number.
